The fixed positional encodings are computed using sine and cosine functions of different frequencies:

\[
\begin{aligned}
PE_{\text{pos},\,2i} &= \sin\!\left(\frac{\text{pos}}{10000^{\,2i/d_{\text{model}}}}\right),\\
PE_{\text{pos},\,2i+1} &= \cos\!\left(\frac{\text{pos}}{10000^{\,2i/d_{\text{model}}}}\right),
\end{aligned}
\]

where \(\text{pos}\) is the position and \(i\) indexes the dimension.  
[attention-is-all-you-need.pdf — Page 6]

The Transformer injects token order by adding **positional encodings** to the input embeddings.  
These encodings are summed with the embeddings at the bottom of the encoder and decoder stacks, so they must have the **same dimensionality as the embeddings**—i.e., the model’s `dmodel` dimension.  

[attention‑is‑all‑you‑need.pdf — Page 6]

claims.claim: The Transformer injects token order by adding positional encodings to the input embeddings.
claims.evidence: Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence. To this end, we add "positional encodings" to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks.

claims.claim: The positional encodings are added at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks.
claims.evidence: we add "positional encodings" to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks.

claims.claim: The positional encodings must have the same dimensionality as the embeddings, i.e., the model's dmodel dimension.
claims.evidence: The positional encodings have the same dimension dmodel as the embeddings, so that the two can be summed.
